current_activity: assembles at Ligneuville, five miles south of Malmédy, for an attack on the town
notes: Event date: night of 20 December 1944 (Cole, ch. 15: the night before the 21 December attack). Event definition: Brought together as a conventional force once the dash to the Meuse bridges was out of the question, the brigade assembles in Ligneuville and reports to the 1st SS Panzer Division headquarters there (Cole, ch. 15; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 15, p. 360: "an enemy force had assembled in Ligneuville, five miles south of Malm"; Wikipedia, Operation Greif: "he was ordered to assemble south of Malmedy". Location: Ligneuville, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole and Wikipedia both name Ligneuville. Commander: Colonel Otto Skorzeny (Cole, ch. 15).

current_activity: attacks Malmédy before dawn in three groups and is repulsed by the US 30th Infantry Division
notes: Event date: 21 December 1944, about two hours before dawn (Cole, ch. 15; Wikipedia). Event definition: Skorzeny divides the brigade into two assault groups and a reserve; the right group strikes north along the Ligneuville road about two hours before dawn; the attack fails, the only noticeable German attempt on Malmédy (Cole, ch. 15; Wikipedia, Operation Greif). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 15, p. 361: "Skorzeny divided his brigade into three groups, two for the assault and one in reserve"; Wikipedia, Operation Greif: "On 21 December 1944 this brigade, under Skorzeny"; "tried to take Malmedy". Location: Malmédy, Liège (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole and Wikipedia both name Malmédy. Commander: Colonel Otto Skorzeny (Cole, ch. 15). Opponents: US 30th Infantry Division.
